edits.old: Speculative decoding changes both execution cost and the numerical history of a quantized runtime. When an application must reproduce a fixed ordinary greedy output, the designer must identify where execution needs constraints and whether the qualified design reduces cost. We study these decisions with natural donor-state crosses, a phase-scoped attention implementation and paid ordinary and matched target-only baselines. CUDA and Vulkan crosses distinguish local current-path, retained-state and interaction effects. A separate B570 fork study finds unchanged immediate decisions but different trajectories under sustained alternate continuation. On RTX, a query-layout transformation retains batched projection and feed-forward work; target prefill and continuation form an inclusion-minimal passing set within a tested four-switch family. The frozen design qualifies full responses on 24 project-unused inputs. Generation speed is 1.170 times ordinary and 1.169 times matched target-only execution. Resident-request speed is 1.742 times ordinary but 1.035 times matched: the draft-free path change already gives 1.683 times. Seven tasks regress against matched request time, and one round reverses direction. Wider fixed-capacity drafting and a B570 endpoint repair qualify while losing performance. Separate M4 and 358H cases test the cost of added control and the limits of draft-only optimization. These results guide constraint placement and the choice to use speculation after qualification, with repair evidence restricted to the tested Qwen3 family and configurations.
edits.new: Speculative decoding changes the numerical history of a quantized runtime as well as its execution cost. When an application requires a fixed ordinary greedy output, the runtime must establish where constraints are needed and whether the qualified design saves time. We connect local state/path diagnosis, phase-scoped repair and measured comparisons with ordinary and matched target-only execution. Natural donor-state crosses on CUDA and Vulkan distinguish current-path, retained-state and interaction effects; a separate B570 fork study shows that immediate agreement can coexist with later divergence. On RTX, a query-layout transformation retains batched projection and feed-forward work. Target prefill and continuation form an inclusion-minimal passing set within a tested four-switch family, and the frozen design qualifies full responses on 24 project-unused inputs. Resident-request speed is 1.742 times ordinary execution; the matched draft-free path already achieves 1.683 times, leaving a 1.035-times speculative increment. Seven tasks regress against matched request time, and one round reverses direction. Wider fixed-capacity drafting and a B570 endpoint repair qualify while losing performance. Auxiliary M4 and 358H cases bound the value of added control and draft-only optimization. These results support a configuration-specific decision process from diagnosis through qualification to cost comparison; repair evidence remains restricted to the tested Qwen3 family.
edits.reason: Focus the abstract on diagnosis, repair and measured cost; retain finite qualification and adverse outcomes. Generation ratios remain in the body.

edits.old: Natural donor-state crosses with own-path controls distinguish local state, path and interaction effects on CUDA and Vulkan. A separate same-state B570 fork study tests the limits of immediate agreement. The RTX query-layout transformation retains batched projection and feed-forward work, and a complete four-switch factorial identifies a sufficient target-phase scope. Paid ordinary/matched/speculative comparisons then determine when a repair, wider draft or added control is useful and when to reject a qualified design.
edits.new: The contribution is a linked diagnosis, repair and cost evaluation within explicit output contracts. Natural donor-state crosses with own-path controls distinguish local state, path and interaction effects on CUDA and Vulkan; a separate same-state B570 fork study establishes the limits of immediate agreement. The RTX query-layout transformation retains batched projection and feed-forward work, and a complete four-switch factorial identifies a sufficient target-phase scope within the tested family. Measured ordinary/matched/speculative comparisons separate the full deployment gain from the speculative increment. B570 supplies a qualified-but-slower counterexample, while the auxiliary M4 and 358H cases delimit the value of added control and draft-only optimization.

edits.old:
\section{Conclusion}
A runtime that must reproduce an ordinary greedy output needs to preserve the stateful transaction as well as its acceptance rule. In the tested RTX implementation, a query-layout change during target prefill and continuation retains other batched work and qualifies a finite full-response panel. Natural crosses motivate that scope, while the complete phase matrix and wider-geometry failures bound it.
edits.new:
\section{Conclusion}
Preserving a fixed ordinary greedy output requires a runtime to account for retained state and current execution, then qualify the complete output under an explicit configuration. In the tested RTX implementation, a query-layout change during target prefill and continuation retains other batched work and qualifies a finite full-response panel. Natural crosses motivate that scope, while the complete phase matrix and wider-geometry failures bound it.
edits.reason: Conclude with the same diagnosis-to-qualification sequence as the abstract.

edits.old: Paid ordinary and matched comparisons then change the performance interpretation: $1.742\times$ RTX request speed includes a $1.683\times$ draft-free target-path gain, leaving $1.035\times$ from speculation on that path. The increment is uneven and reverses in one round. A wider qualified draft loses, B570 endpoint repair remains slower than strong baselines, and the separate M4/358H cases constrain the value of added control and draft-only optimization. Within the studied family, the operating decision follows local diagnosis, complete-output qualification under an explicit configuration and paid comparison with both baselines.
edits.new: Measured cost determines whether the qualified design is useful. The RTX request speed is $1.742\times$ ordinary execution; the draft-free target path already gives $1.683\times$, and speculation adds $1.035\times$ relative to that matched path. The increment is uneven and reverses in one round. A wider qualified draft loses, B570 endpoint repair remains slower than strong baselines, and the auxiliary M4/358H cases constrain the value of added control and draft-only optimization. These findings support local diagnosis, configuration-specific qualification and measurement against both baselines. They do not establish repair beyond the tested Qwen3 family, superiority to external methods under the same contract, or stability across independent sessions.
edits.reason: State the cost interpretation precisely and close on the three acknowledged evidence limits.
